To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the erythroid specific activation is due to a combination of positive and negative regulatory elements.

(i) the 5'flanking region of the Xenopus alpha-globin genes contain erythroid specific enhancer(s), (ii) the alpha-globins genes are activated by erythroid specific transcription factors, (iii) the alpha-gene enhancers are located between position -1.5 and -0.5 kb relative to the transcription start site.
the erythroid specific transcription factor NF-E2 binds to a site located in the proximal promoter of the Xenopus alpha-globin genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms involved in erythroid specific expression of the adult alpha and beta globin genes in Xenopus laeavis.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the control of gene expression in the erythroid lineage.
the regulation of the adult globin genes of Xenopus laeavis, the South African clawed toad.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adult alpha-goblin promoter is active in X. laeivs erythroblasts and is stimulated by erythroid specific transcription factors.
erythroid-specific transcription factors can be activated by fusion of erythroblasts with nonerythroid cells.
erythroblasts contain factors which activate transcription from a promoter that is not normally expressed in erythroblasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the erythroid specific activation is mediated by a combination of factors that are both erythroid specific and ubiquitous in the cell.
the alpha-globine promoter is active in kidney cells but that erythroid-specific trans-acting factors are required for maximal expression.
we have identified a trans-acting factor that is erythroid specific and is able to activate the adult alpha-gene promoter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the erythroid-specific activation of the alpha-globins promoter can be achieved in heterokaryons between X. laevas kidney cells and X. laeavis erythroblasts.
the erythroid specific factors that activate the adult alpha-glb promoter are present at low levels in the kidney cells and that their levels increase after fusion.
we can now use transient heterokaryon assays in Xenopus to study erythroid specific gene regulation.
